title: a module-level initialization trust claim does not confer call-site trust on the module's exports
notes:
specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Foreign Boundary' (Locked): "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration. Trusted `@throws {never}` metadata opts out; `@throws {T}` declares a more precise channel." The subject of that sentence is the CALL, so the claim covers what the call does with an argument it was handed. specification/requirements.mdx, 'Scoping' (Locked), assigns the deferred half elsewhere: "Imported JavaScript or TypeScript that starts hidden background work owns that work. Caller-controlled background APIs MUST expose explicit completion or disposal handles through their adapters." And specification/failures.mdx, 'Panic Does Not Widen a Return Type', is why the third reading — that the callback must independently be panic-free — is not available at all: every `.vibe` function may abort with `panic(...)` while keeping a plain return type, so panic-freedom is not spellable and a rule demanding it would admit nothing. The module claim answers a different question — may this edge be imported at all (VIBE1510) — and has never doubled as a per-call opt-out. Without this case, a lane widening the argument-position rule could let the module header confer call-site trust, which would open every export of every trusted module at once. 09-foreign-calls/module-init-trust-is-not-a-function-level-throws-claim pins the same separation for a non-callback call. The declared VIBE1101 is the reason this case carries an xfail: see the marker.

2026-09-07 retirement: measured as XPASS in the full native-only corpus run. The native boundary reporter now charges Panic to the enclosing row before inference, so both profiles report the complete authored diagnostic list, including VIBE1101. No source, required code, position or message assertion was removed.
